Government Advocate  Mr.Su.Srinivas for R4
COMMON ORDER
Since the issue involved in this writ petition are one and the same, they are heard together and disposed of by way of this common order.
2. These writ petitions are filed for a direction to the 1st respondent/District Collector being the arbitrator in land acquisition matters to dispose of the appeal filed by the writ petitioners.

3. The petitioners submitted appeals on 25.03.2024 and 03.02.2024 respectively under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act 1956 before the first respondent, however, the same are pending without consideration.
Hence, these writ petitions.

4. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis WP.Nos.12504 & 12510 of 2024 5.
By consent of both parties, these writ petitions are taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

6. Considering the limited relief sought for in these writ petitions, the first respondent is directed to consider the appeal filed by the petitioners dated 25.03.2024 and 13.02.2024 respectively and pass appropriate orders by disposing of the petitioner's appeal on merits considering the provisions contained under the National Highways Act, 1956.
Such exercise shall be completed within a period of two months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
7. With the above direction, these writ petitions are disposed of.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition stands closed.
